verses.1: For the choir director. A psalm of David. O God, do not be silent about my praise.
verses.2: For the mouth of the wicked and the mouth of deceit have opened against me; they spoke against me with a lying tongue.
verses.3: And words of hatred surrounded me, and they waged war against me without cause.
verses.4: Because of my love, they entangled me, but I offered prayer.
verses.5: And they placed evil upon me in place of good, and hatred in place of my love.
verses.6: Send a wicked one against him, and let a deceiver stand at his right hand.
verses.7: When he is judged, let the wicked be found guilty, and may his prayer become a sin.
verses.8: May his days be few, and may another take his office.
verses.9: May his children be orphans, and his wife a widow.
verses.10: May his children wander as beggars and be driven from their ruins.
verses.11: May the creditor seize everything he has, and may strangers plunder his labor.
verses.12: May there be no one to show him kindness, nor to be a father to his orphans.
verses.13: May his descendants be destroyed, and in one generation may his name be blotted out.
verses.14: May the sin of his fathers be remembered before the LORD, and may the iniquity of his mother not be erased.
verses.15: May they be before the LORD always, and may his name be cut off from the earth.
verses.16: Because he did not remember to show kindness, and he pursued the poor and the needy and the broken-hearted to destroy them.
verses.17: And he loved curses, and they will come to him; and he did not want a blessing, and it will remain far from him.
verses.18: And he clothed himself with curses as a garment, and they will come into him like water within his inner parts and like oil in his bones.
verses.19: May this be to him as a garment he puts on, and as a belt with which he constantly girds himself.
verses.20: This is the work of those who slander me, by the LORD, and those who speak evil against my soul.
verses.21: And you, O LORD, Lord, deal with me for the sake of your name, for your steadfast love is good, deliver me.
verses.22: For I am poor and needy, and my heart is broken within me.
verses.23: I was like a shadow when it is cast down; I was shaken like a locust.
verses.24: My knees gave way from fasting, and my flesh was wasted away from oil.
verses.25: And I have become a disgrace to them; they saw me, they wagged their heads.
verses.26: Help me, O LORD my God, save me according to your great steadfast love.
verses.27: And let them know that your hand is this, and you, O LORD, have done it.
verses.28: Let them curse, but you bless; let them rise up and be put to shame, but your servant will rejoice.
verses.29: Let my adversaries be clothed with disgrace, and let them be covered with shame as with a mantle.
verses.30: I will greatly praise the LORD with my mouth, and in the midst of many I will extol him.
verses.31: For he stands at the right hand of the poor, to save from those who condemn his life.

notes:
Notes
- v. 1: "For the choir director" is a translation of "לַמְנַצֵּחַ" (to the chief musician), a common heading in psalms.
- v. 21: "And you, O LORD, Lord" reflects the doubling of the divine name in "יְהוִה אֲדֹנָי", translated here as "the LORD Lord".
- v. 27: "you bless" and "your servant" follow the contextual shift from the psalmist's curses to a plea for divine blessing.
- v. 31: "to save from those who condemn his life" captures the meaning of "לְהוֹשִׁיעַ מִשֹּׁפְטֵי נַפְשֽׁוֹ", translating "shoftay" as "those who condemn" rather than "judges" to maintain the context of persecution.
